Article Title: Paralympic star Lauren Steadman seals Celebrity MasterChef crown after nail-biting finale
Article Text:
Lauren Steadman. Image via: BBC

Lauren Steadman beats Celebrity MasterChef rivals in dramatic final showdown

Lauren Steadman's Celebrity MasterChef win adds to a long sporting résumé

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lauren Steadman has won Celebrity MasterChef, and the Paralympic champion needed every single course to do it. Three finalists cooked a three-course meal for judges Grace Dent and Giorgio Locatelli on Friday night, and only one could lift the 2026 trophy.The BBC One final capped a contest that began with 15 celebrities. Olympic medallist Emily Campbell and Love Island's Shakira Khan pushed hard, and Dent found the choice close to impossible. One dessert tipped the verdict, though, and a runner-up had a joke ready afterwards.Lauren Steadman took the title on Friday, September 18, in a final shown on BBC One and iPlayer at 8 p.m. The Paralympic gold medallist beat Campbell and Khan in a head-to-head where each finalist had to cook and present a faultless three-course meal. It was the last chance to show passion and creativity in front of Dent and Locatelli, and Steadman's execution earned her the trophy.Steadman opened with scallops pan-fried in chilli butter, served with a coconut and spinach lentil dahl puree and topped with fresh apple batons. The main was a beef wellington with truffle mash, caramelised shallot, butternut squash puree, tenderstem broccoli and a red wine jus. Dessert was a classic sticky toffee pudding with dates, caramel sauce and clotted cream ice cream.The pudding did the most damage. Locatelli said, "Mamma mia... this is the best sticky toffee pudding I've ever had." Dent went with "exemplary" for the same dish and said the final plates were simply wonderful. Locatelli also explained the bigger picture. Steadman has a knack for turning every situation into an advantage, and that is why the crown went to the champion.Finals week added plenty of pressure. Steadman made a dog bone shaped dessert for fifty guests at Crufts, billed as the world's largest and most prestigious dog show. The Chef's Table at The Ritz, a top event on the culinary calendar, was another test.After the win, Steadman said, "This is up there with a Paralympic gold medal." Speechless moments are rare, Steadman added, and this was one of them.Steadman is an MBE, was born in Peterborough and is a University of Portsmouth graduate. Swimming came first, at the 2008 Beijing Paralympics at age 15 and again at London 2012. Paratriathlon followed, bringing silver in Rio 2016, gold in Tokyo and bronze in Paris 2024. The three-time world champion is also an eight-time European champion.Steadman reached the Strictly Come Dancing semi-finals in 2018 as the show's first female contestant with a disability, then finished as a finalist on Celebrity SAS: Who Dares Wins in 2019.The kitchen was a different kind of risk, and Steadman knew it. Before the series, the athlete told the BBC that sport had taught pressure handling and a love of new challenges. Cooking for loved ones is one thing, Steadman said, and having food critically analysed is another. The show could go very wrong, but it might also build confidence. Steadman calls the style intuitive. A soup that got far too many stock cubes once became a pasta sauce, and measuring is rarely part of the routine.The other finalists took defeat well. Campbell called the result "more than deserved" and joked about being relieved that the contest was over. Khan, a runner-up on Love Island last year, said, "Always the bridesmaid, never the bride." She added that she had a ball and called Steadman's cooking a gold medal performance.
Article Summary: Paralympic swimmer lauren steadman wins celebrity masterchef 2026. Steadman beat olympic medallist emily campbell and love island's shakira khan. The three-time world champion is also an eight-time european champion. The bbc one final capped a contest that began with 15 celebrities.

Article Title: At 13, Quimcy Dsouza was a middle-distance runner before football took over; 11 years later, Ronaldinho-inspired Teqball has put her one win away from Asian Games history
Article Text:
India's Quimcy Joaquim Dsouza (Image: @quimcyyy/Instagram)

From middle-distance running to football and Teqball

Seven-time national champion and international trailblazer

Quimcy Dsouza ’s Asian Games 2026 campaign

Quimcy falls short in semifinal against Indonesia

Bronze medal match offers chance to make history

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s Quimcy Joaquim Dsouza suffered a 1-2 defeat to Indonesia’s Ima Sumaya in the women’s singles Teqball semifinal at the Asian Games 2026 on Saturday. However, her medal hopes remain alive, with the 24-year-old set to compete for bronze against Japan’s Yuina Sakamoto on Sunday.A victory would make Quimcy the first Indian to win a Teqball medal at the Asian Games, where the sport is making its debut at the Aichi-Nagoya edition. The Indian’s journey to the last four has already been a breakthrough, marking an important chapter in her rise as one of the country’s leading Teqball players.Hailing from Mumbai, Quimcy began her sporting journey as a middle-distance runner at the age of 13 as reported by The Indian Express. Her passion for football soon took over, and she went on to represent Maharashtra in age-group football.Although her football career did not progress as she had hoped, her love for the game remained. After completing a degree in Sports Management, she joined sports goods retailer Decathlon and discovered Teqball after watching Brazilian football legend Ronaldinho play the sport in Instagram videos.Quimcy took up the sport and gradually established herself as a leading figure in India’s Teqball community.Quimcy became the first Indian woman Teqer to represent the country at the international level. She also founded the Teqball Club of Bengaluru to help promote the sport at the grassroots level.A seven-time national champion, she has emerged as one of the trailblazers of Indian Teqball. Earlier in 2026, she finished ninth at the Teqball World Championships in Romania, further strengthening her credentials on the international stage. Her performances at the Asian Games have now given her an opportunity to add a historic medal to her achievements.Quimcy made an impressive start to her Asian Games debut, topping Group A with two wins to secure direct qualification for the women’s singles semifinals.She opened her campaign with a 2-1 comeback victory over top-seeded Japan’s Yuina Sakamoto. After losing the first set 10-12, Quimcy fought back to win the second 12-11 before clinching the decider 13-11. She then defeated Cambodia’s Koemyean DY 12-9, 12-7 in straight sets to finish at the top of her group and book a place in the last four.Quimcy started her semifinal against Indonesia’s Ima Sumaya on a strong note, winning the opening set 12-7. Sumaya responded in the second, recovering from an early deficit to take it 12-9 and force a decider.The Indian raced to a 3-0 lead in the third set and extended it to 4-1. However, Sumaya mounted a comeback, took control of the decider and won it 12-7 to secure her place in the final. The defeat ended Quimcy’s hopes of reaching the gold-medal match, but she will have another opportunity to finish her debut Asian Games campaign on the podium.Quimcy will face Japan’s Yuina Sakamoto in Sunday’s bronze-medal match. The Indian had defeated Sakamoto in the group stage, but will need to reproduce that performance to secure a place on the podium.A win would earn India its first-ever Teqball medal at the Asian Games. Quimcy has also competed in mixed doubles alongside Mohamed Anas Imran Beg. The Indian pair defeated the Philippines’ Jhoana Abulencia and Prince Agustin in their Group A opener.Teqball, invented in Hungary, combines elements of football and table tennis and is played on a curved table. The sport is making its Asian Games debut at Aichi-Nagoya 2026, with five medal events: men’s and women’s singles, men’s and women’s doubles, and mixed doubles.

A victory would make quimcy the first indian to win a teqball medal at the asian games. The indian pair defeated the philippines’ jhoana abulencia and prince agustin in their group a opener.

Article Title: How Andy Reid keeps finding immediate value in rookies while the Chiefs continue building a dominant defense
Article Text:
Andy Reid’s rookie secret revealed (Getty Images)

How does Andy Reid get immediate production from rookies so consistently?

Can the Chiefs' defense sustain this level of play through the full season?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Kansas City's defense turned heads in Week 1 against Denver, and not just because of the outcome. The story was who was doing the damage. Several young, first-year players showed up ready, contributing in ways that had ESPN analyst Daniel Jeremiah reaching for superlatives after reviewing the film. With the Colts coming up next on the schedule, that rookie-fueled unit is already generating serious conversation around the league.The short answer, according to Jeremiah, is coaching. But it goes deeper than that."I thought the Chiefs' defense, when you dug in and watched the tape with so many new pieces and young pieces, I thought they played outstanding," Jeremiah said on ESPN's BigDay show. "From R Mason Thomas off the edge, Peter Woods inside. You saw [Mansoor] Delane with a pick before he got injured. A lot of young pieces, and this has long been one of the best teaching staffs in the NFL. And Steve Spagnolo and that group did a good job getting those young guys ready to go. So I'm a believer in this Chiefs defense."That last line matters. Jeremiah is not someone who hands out compliments loosely, especially this early in a season. What he saw on tape was not raw talent masking poor technique.These were young players executing within a system, which is a credit to how Kansas City's staff builds its install process from the ground up.Reid and defensive coordinator Steve Spagnolo have built a culture around detailed preparation. Rookies in Kansas City do not get eased in quietly. They get pushed into the fire with enough coaching support behind them that they rarely get burned badly. It is a model that has paid off repeatedly, and Week 1 showed it is still working.That is the real question hanging over this team right now. Performing well in Week 1 is one thing. Doing it across 17 games with a roster carrying this much youth on the defensive side is something else entirely.Mansoor Delane's injury is already a concern. He picked off a pass before leaving the game, and losing a young corner with that kind of instinct is not something you shrug off. The Chiefs will need other pieces to hold up.On the offensive side, Jeremiah noted that things were not completely smooth either. "Offensively, yes, they ran the ball well, particularly from under center," he said. "I don't think the pass game was super synced up yet. Patrick's still more comfortable in the gun and some of that's just, you know, it's always been done. And I also think there's some of the, you know, coming off the knee injury, it's just more natural for him.So the offense is still finding its rhythm, which means the defense cannot afford to slip. Kenneth Walker III had a strong showing, and Patrick Mahomes will sharpen as the weeks go by. But right now, Kansas City is leaning on that young defensive group to carry more of the load than people expected.If those rookies keep delivering, the Chiefs will be a very difficult team to plan against come January.

Several young, first-year players showed up ready, contributing in ways that had espn analyst daniel jeremiah reaching for superlatives. With the colts coming up next on the schedule, that rookie-fueled unit is generating serious conversation.

Article Title: Chess Olympiad Round 3: Koneru Humpy downs 'Greek Goddess' Tsolakidou; Gukesh back above 2700
Article Text:
Koneru Humpy and Gukesh (Photo by Rafal Oleksiewicz and Michal Walusza from FIDE)

Gukesh back to winning ways

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India's winning streaks stay intact

NEW DELHI: On Friday, the Indian women's team, defending champions and unbeaten so far in the tournament, was paired against Greece in Round 3 of the 2026 Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. On paper, this looked routine. India, the top seeds, were expected to win the tie, and they eventually did. But the top-board clash between Koneru Humpy and Greece's Stavroula Tsolakidou carried a subplot that had been building for a fortnight, and it turned an otherwise straightforward fixture into the day's most closely watched game.Tsolakidou was part of Ganges Grandmasters, the eventual champions of the just-concluded Global Chess League (GCL) Season 4 . It was against Humpy, playing for APL Pipers, that Tsolakidou suffered her first loss of that tournament, playing white.To turn the tables in the reverse fixture, she needed something special, and got it when coach Adhiban Baskaran handed her a folder titled "Prep for the Greek Goddess!" Working off that file, she beat Humpy with the black pieces. The moniker "Greek Goddess" became famous.The two met again in the GCL final, where Tsolakidou held Humpy to a draw in the first game and then beat her again with black in the second.A positive score over the Indian, coupled with the results on the other boards, was enough to hand Ganges Grandmasters the title, with Tsolakidou also named the Player of the Tournament.So when the pairing brought them together again on Friday, it was more than a Grandmaster-versus-International Master matchup. This time, as the format shifted from rapid to classical, the Indian veteran Grandmaster prevailed.39-year-old Humpy, with white, built her position with patience. The game began as a Nimzo-Indian structure, with Humpy choosing an ambitious setup featuring 10.b4 and 11.b5, gaining queenside space.Black’s pieces became somewhat passive, while White gradually built pressure with 14.f4, 15.Qf3 and 16.Rad1.The critical phase arrived with 21.e5, opening lines and increasing the activity of White’s pieces.After 22.bxc6 bxc6, Humpy’s knight penetrated with 23.Ne4 and 24.Nxd6, winning material and creating tactical threats.The sequence 25.Nxe8 Rxe8 26.Qxh4 left White with a significant advantage, although Black’s active queen and passed-pawn kept the doors slightly open for a comeback.Humpy maintained the initiative, coordinating her rooks and bishop. 40.e6 was particularly strong, leading to 41.Bxe6+ and 42.Rd7+.After winning the f5-bishop with 43.Bxf5, White’s material and attacking advantage became decisive. Tsolakidou resigned after 46.Rf1, capping off a perfect day for the Indian Grandmaster, who had taken a rest against Finland in Round 2.In the open section, world champion D Gukesh made his way back to winning ways after Thursday's rating dip below 2700, a drop that had made headlines less for its size than for whom it happened to.Playing black against Italy's Sabino Brunello on Friday, Gukesh met a Queen's Indian-style setup.After 4...Ba6 and 5...c5, Black immediately challenged White’s queenside structure and achieved active piece play. The game became highly tactical once Gukesh expanded with 15...g5 and centralized strongly with 17...Ne4 and 19...Nd4.Brunello tried to simplify with 21.Nxd4 and 22.Rxc8, but Black’s pieces remained more active. The key sequence began with 23...Nc3, forcing exchanges that improved Black’s bishop activity. After 25...Re5, Gukesh increased the pressure, and 26...Bxe2 won an important pawn while keeping White’s king exposed.28...Bxh3 removed a key defender, while 29...Bd4+ and 30...Re2+ drove the king into a dangerous position. 31...Qxh3 left Black with overwhelming attacking threats and a large material advantage.Although Brunello gave checks with 32.Qxg5+ and 33.Qd8+, they were only temporary. Gukesh's queen and bishop combined to set up mating threats, and Brunello resigned after 33 moves, handing Gukesh a much-needed win and, with it, a step back towards the 2700 mark he had slipped under just a day earlier.The rest of India's open team also had a strong day against Italy. Praggnanandhaa and Erigaisi both drew their games, but Nihal Sarin added another win to his growing tally, beating Francesco Sonis, as India closed out the match 3-1.For India's women, Friday's 3.5-0.5 win over Greece, with only Divya Deshmukh drawing her game against Anastasia Avramidou, kept an already imposing unbeaten run alive, with Humpy, Vantika Agrawal, and Savitha Shri all winning their individual games. Vaishali Rameshbabu took a rest day.ALSO READ: The silver medal Koneru Humpy's 9-year-old daughter will remember as gold Both Indian teams will be back in action on Saturday, with the open side facing Spain and the women's team taking on Mongolia.
Article Summary: India's koneru humpy beats greece's stavroula tsolakidou in round 3 of the 2026 chess olympiad in samarkand, uzbekistan. The indian veteran grandmaster prevailed as the format shifted from rapid to classical. World champion d gukesh made his way back to winning ways after thursday's rating dip below 2700.

Article Title: Sophie Cunningham gives her honest take on Sydney Sweeney’s highly controversial ad
Article Text:
Sophie Cunningham shares her take on Sydney Sweeney’s controversial ad. Image via: Getty Images

Sophie Cunningham joins Sydney Sweeney ad debate with her take

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Why was Sydney Sweeney's ad controversial?

Sophie Cunningham isn't one to stay quiet, and this week she finally weighed in on the Sydney Sweeney gambling ad controversy that's had social media buzzing for days. The Indiana Fever guard tackled the topic on her podcast, calling out the campaign while still leaving room to defend Sweeney's right to cash in on her fame.Cunningham admitted she wasn't a fan of how the ad played out, questioning its authenticity from the jump. But she wasn't interested in piling on the actress either. Here's what she actually said, and why the ad drew so much heat in the first place.Sophie Cunningham addressed the ongoing chatter this week, tackling it head-on during an episode of her podcast, No Hesitation With Sophie Cunningham & Drew Hanlen. She said her phone had been flooded with texts and comments from people begging her to share an opinion, so she decided it was finally time.Her first question cut straight to the point: does Sweeney even gamble on sports? "Like it's just so unauthentic," she said, laying out her skepticism about the whole campaign. Cunningham wasn't shocked by how Sweeney chose to represent the brand, noting it's simply the kind of marketing the actress has built her career on."I have so many takes, but first of all, does she even gamble on sports? Like, it's just so inauthentic.Now, here's my hot take… Why are girls mad? Like, that is literally what she does. Why is anyone mad? Like… of course that's going to draw attention,” the Fever guard shared.Still, she made clear she wasn't thrilled with this particular execution, admitting she wondered what exactly the ad was trying to accomplish. Again, do I agree with it? “Morally, I think it's kind of weird, but like, to each their own. Go do your thing, sis," Cunningham added.She also pushed back on the backlash itself, wondering aloud why so many women were upset over something that's essentially just Sweeney doing what she's always done. Cunningham called the outrage a little confusing, though she said she understood why some found the ad morally odd. Despite her criticism, she was quick to add that she genuinely likes Sweeney and doesn't think women should tear each other down over choices like this.Her closing message was simple: let Sweeney make her money and do her thing.The commercial in question features Sweeney posing in minimal clothing alongside sports equipment to promote a sports prediction platform, a visual pairing that got people talking almost instantly. Several athletes felt the ad leaned entirely on Sweeney's image rather than any genuine connection to sports or gambling, and that rubbed plenty of fans the wrong way.Sweeney responded to some of the criticism by sharing photos of male and female athletes who had posed n*de for ESPN The Magazine, seemingly drawing a comparison to her own shoot.
Article Summary: Sophie cunningham addressed the sydney sweeney gambling ad controversy on her podcast. The indiana fever guard questioned the authenticity of the campaign. She also questioned why so many women were upset over something sweeney has always done. Despite her criticism, she said she genuinely likes sweeney and doesn't think women should tear each other down.

NEW DELHI: World champion D Gukesh has offered some context behind Arjun Erigaisi’s shock defeat in the opening round of the Chess Olympiad, saying India’s players had endured a hectic start to the tournament and were left waiting for hours to get their rooms.Arjun, India’s second-ranked player, suffered a surprise defeat against Thailand’s 2363-rated International Master Prin Laohawirapap on Board 1. The 23-year-old, playing with the white pieces, had a winning position at different stages but eventually faltered in the endgame.Gukesh said the team’s difficult arrival and accommodation issues had affected the players.“Arjun’s first game was very unfortunate, but also worth mentioning that we had a very hectic travel and then the first day there were some organisation issues,” Gukesh said in an interview with FIDE after his Round 3 win over Italy's Sabino Brunello.“So like Arjun got a room probably a few hours before he went. I mean, we all waited for like six hours to get a room. So obviously the first round Arjun, he was just tired and he blundered in the end.”The world champion added that the situation had improved since the opening day and the players were now better rested.“The first day was a bit tricky for all of us, but after that, I think we are all rested. We are all looking forward to the games and all good,” he said.Gukesh was also asked about India’s decision to field him on Board 4, rather than the top board. He said the team’s priority was to choose the order that gave India the best chance of winning the tournament.“I think it’s pretty clear that Pragg and Arjun have been in really good shape. Also, the rating says the same,” Gukesh said. “It was my idea and also the whole team, we all thought the same that this is the order that gives us the best chance of winning the tournament.”ALSO READ: Chess Olympiad Round 3: Koneru Humpy downs 'Greek Goddess' Tsolakidou; Gukesh back above 2700 The 20-year-old said he had no issue with playing on Board 4 despite being the reigning world champion, stressing that the team’s interests came first.“If the team needs it, I would even rest all the games. So I think we are here playing for India and there’s no player bigger than the country. I’m just happy to do whatever it takes for the team to do well,” he said.India, still unbeaten in both sections, will next face Spain in the open section, while the Indian women’s team will take on Mongolia.
Article Summary: World champion d gukesh says india's players had a hectic start to the chess olympiad. He said the team’s difficult arrival and accommodation issues had affected the players. Arjun erigaisi suffered a surprise defeat in the opening round of the tournament.

India Women produced a dominant all-round performance to thrash Japan by eight wickets in the quarter-finals of the 2026 Asian Games, booking their place in the semi-finals against Bangladesh.The result also sets up a repeat of the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 semi-final line-up, with Sri Lanka set to face Pakistan in the other last-four clash.After winning the toss and opting to field, India’s bowlers dismantled Japan’s batting line-up, restricting the hosts to just 57 in 19.5 overs. Shree Charani led the charge with a remarkable spell of 4/10, including two maiden overs, to register the best bowling figures by an Indian at the Asian Games. Shafali Verma also chipped in with two wickets for 13 runs.Ayaka Kato-Stafford top-scored for Japan with 25 off 47 balls, but the hosts struggled to build partnerships against India’s disciplined attack.India’s chase was emphatic, as they reached the target in just five overs, finishing at 59/2 and winning with 90 balls to spare. Shafali Verma set the tone with a blistering 40 off 15 balls, striking six fours and two sixes.She hammered four boundaries in the opening over and later sealed the victory with a six off Shimako Kato.India had promoted Kamalini and Fulmali up the order, but the move did not pay off, with Kamalini dismissed for a duck and Fulmali scoring six. Shafali then combined with Richa Ghosh, who came in at No. 4, to complete the chase in a hurry.The pair shared a warm hug after the winning hit before crossing over to greet the Japanese players. Japan’s two wickets offered a small positive from an otherwise difficult outing.
Article Summary: India beat japan by 8 wickets, set up semi-final against bangladesh. Shree charani stars as japan are bowled out for 57 in 19.5 overs. Shafali verma and richa ghosh wrap up chase in five overs.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge

El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit

El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Cristiano Ronaldo: "I don't think a tournament of six or seven games can determine whether you're the best player in…"
Article Text:
Cristiano Ronaldo

Quote of the day by Cristiano Ronaldo

"I don't think a tournament of six or seven games can determine whether you're the best player in the world or not."

Written by the player the debate is actually about

Why this argument keeps resurfacing in sports more broadly

A simple way to actually use this idea

Other quotes by Cristiano Ronaldo

"I disagree [that Messi is better]. I don't want to be humble."

"The last interview that we made was hard, honest, like always. This is what I pretend to do with my interviews."

"But I think my story not will change. A lot will be similar."

Two people can look at the same career and weigh its achievements using completely different scales. One treats a small number of high-stakes tournament results, especially a World Cup title, as the single decisive measure of greatness, the tiebreaker that settles any debate regardless of everything else on the résumé. The other argues that a handful of knockout matches, played across a single month every four years, is too small and too dependent on circumstance, teammates, injuries, refereeing decisions, a single bad bounce, to serve as the ultimate verdict on an individual player's quality across an entire career. Ronaldo made this second argument directly in his November 2025 interview with Piers Morgan, responding to the ongoing public debate over whether he or Lionel Messi, who won the World Cup with Argentina in 2022, deserves to be considered the greater player of the two.What makes this line worth examining closely is exactly who is making the argument and why. Ronaldo has won five Ballon d'Or awards, multiple Champions League titles, and is men's football's all-time leading international goalscorer, an extraordinarily decorated career by almost any measure. The one major honor missing from that list is a World Cup title, the exact trophy Messi secured in 2022, an achievement widely treated in football discourse as the single most important item separating the two players' legacies in the ongoing "greatest of all time" debate.That context matters for reading the quote fairly. It's a genuinely defensible position, shared by plenty of football analysts, that a single-elimination tournament compressed into a few weeks is a noisy, luck-influenced way to measure individual greatness compared to sustained excellence across fifteen or twenty club seasons. It's also true that the argument happens to benefit Ronaldo specifically, coming from the one player in the debate who doesn't have the trophy in question. Both things can be true simultaneously: the argument has real merit on its own terms, and it is also, unavoidably, being made by someone with an obvious personal stake in which measure of greatness wins out.This isn't a debate unique to football. Similar arguments play out across nearly every team sport, where fans and pundits argue over whether a player who never won a championship can still be considered among the greatest, weighed against a less statistically dominant player who happened to win more titles, often with considerably better supporting teammates around them. Basketball has run some version of this argument for decades. So has tennis, cricket, and American football. The underlying tension Ronaldo names, individual excellence versus team-dependent outcomes, is a genuinely unresolved question in how sports greatness gets measured, not simply a convenient excuse invented for this one specific case.The useful move here is noticing when someone's argument, however genuinely defensible on its own logic, also happens to serve their own interests, and weighing the argument on its merits rather than dismissing or accepting it purely based on who's making it. A fair test, when evaluating any claim, is to ask whether it would still hold up if made by someone with no personal stake in the outcome. That question won't settle every argument. It usually clarifies how much of the case rests on genuine logic and how much rests on convenient timing.
Article Summary: Cristiano ronaldo said he doesn't think a tournament can determine whether you're the best player in the world. He was responding to the ongoing debate over whether he or lionel messi is the greater player of the two. The argument has real merit on its own terms, and it is also made by someone with an obvious personal stake in which measure of greatness wins out.

The PNB MetLife Junior Badminton Championship is not just about records; it’s about fostering a culture of healthy living, determination, and resilience among the future champions of the sport.In the words of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy, the championship serves as an invaluable platform.---------------------------------------------------------------As we celebrate the successful culmination of the 7th edition of PNB MetLife Junior Badminton Championship , we take pride in surpassing our own world record for highest participation and for being recognized by World Record Certification Agency. Beyond the records, JBC represents a significant milestone in our mission to lay the groundwork for India’ s glory and success on the international badminton stage by creating a pan-India badminton ecosystem that nurtures champions at the grassroots levelThis year has been especially remarkable for PNB MetLife JBC as we joined hands with world champions Chirag Shetty and Satwiksairaj Rankireddy as JBC Mentors for the young talents associated with this tournament. Article Title: Sega is bringing back Crazy Taxi after years; New World Tour game gets playable demo at Tokyo Game Show 2026
Article Text:
Sega is reviving Crazy Taxi with a new open-world game

Crazy Taxi World Tour demo at Tokyo Game Show

What to expect from the new Crazy Taxi game

Crazy Taxi gets multiplayer modes

From reveal to Tokyo Game Show 2026

"All I Want",

Crazy Taxi World Tour release platforms

Crazy Taxi World Tour has been confirmed for 2027. Japanese gaming major Sega has announced that the new game in its long-running Crazy Taxi franchise will be playable at Tokyo Game Show 2026, giving fans their first major hands-on opportunity. The game will be showcased at Sega/Atlus’ booth at Makuhari Messe in Chiba, Japan, from September 17 to September 21.This marks the return of the Crazy Taxi series with a new open-world game featuring both single-player and multiplayer modes. The public can access the event from September 19 to September 21, while Sega will also host dedicated stage events around the game.Crazy Taxi World Tour will have a dedicated area at the Sega/Atlus booth in Hall 4-N01. Visitors can try an arcade-style demo using a racing wheel and also take photos with a life-size replica of Axel’s taxi.Sega has scheduled two-stage events for the game. The Mission Challenge will be on September 17 and the Demo Playthrough on September 19. Both events will also be streamed live on Sega's YouTube channel.Crazy Taxi World Tour follows the series' protagonist, Axel, as he travels across five cities worldwide.The story begins after a masked international crew steals his taxi, sending Axel on a chase across different locations.Gameplay retains the core Crazy Taxi formula of picking up passengers and getting to destinations quickly, but adds an open-world setting. Players can also make money through performing aerial stunts and odd jobs.The game will also include a classic time-attack Arcade Mode and vehicle customisation options.Sega is adding cross-platform multiplayer to the new Crazy Taxi game. Players will be able to compete in two modes called Pickup Race and Cops 'N' Cabbies.Both modes will support Ranked Match, which uses automatic matchmaking, and Custom Match, which allows players to create private lobbies and change gameplay rules.Sega first revealed Crazy Taxi World Tour during the Xbox Games Showcase in June. Series creator Kenji Kanno is returning as director. The reveal trailer also featured The Offspring’s songconnecting the new title with the music-driven identity of the original Crazy Taxi.Ahead of Tokyo Game Show, Sega held a closed network test from September 11 to September 13. The test allowed selected players to try the Pickup Race and Cops 'N' Cabbies multiplayer modes.Sega has also confirmed that generative AI tools were used as a support aid during development. However, the company said it did not use the technology for the game’s voice performers.Crazy Taxi World Tour is scheduled to launch in 2027. It will be available on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Xbox on PC, Nintendo Switch 2 and PC through Steam. The Tokyo Game Show demo gives players an early look at Sega’s return to the Crazy Taxi franchise before its full release next year.
Article Summary: Crazy taxi world tour will be playable at tokyo game show 2026. The game will be showcased at sega/atlus’ booth at makuhari messe in chiba. The public can access the event from september 19 to september 21. Sega will also host dedicated stage events around the game.
